hindi: वास्तविक संख्या $k$ के लिए माना कि $p,q,r:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $p(x)=x^{2}+1$, $q(x)=x^{2}+x$ तथा $r(x)=2x^{2}+kx+k^{2}$ द्वारा परिभाषित हैं। तब $k$ के उन सभी वास्तविक मानों का योग, जिनके लिए
solution: Each row is (coefficients of $x^{2},x,1$) times the columns $(j^{2},j,1)$, $j=1,2,3$; the column determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1&4&9\\1&2&3\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=-2\ne0$
So the determinant is $0\iff$ one row is a linear combination of the others $\iff r=\lambda p+\mu q$
solution_full: For a polynomial $s(x)=ax^{2}+bx+c$ the row $(s(1),s(2),s(3))$ equals $a(1,4,9)+b(1,2,3)+c(1,1,1)$.
Hence the determinant equals $\begin{vmatrix}1&0&1\\1&1&0\\2&k&k^{2}\end{vmatrix}\cdot\begin{vmatrix}1&4&9\\1&2&3\\1&1&1\end{vmatrix}$ (rows of coefficients times the rows $(j^{2}),(j),(1)$).

So the determinant is $-2(k^{2}+k-2)$. It vanishes exactly when the coefficient rows are dependent, that is when $r$ is a linear combination $\lambda p+\mu q$: $\mu=k$ ($x$-coefficient), $\lambda=k^{2}$ (constant), $\lambda+\mu=2$ ($x^{2}$-coefficient).
Check for $k=1$: rows $(2,5,10)$, $(2,6,12)$, $(4,11,22)$, and the third is the sum of the first two.
The sum of the values is $1+(-2)=-1$. The product $-2$ is option (C).
originality_note: New: a determinant of values of three quadratics at 1, 2, 3 vanishes exactly when one quadratic is a combination of the other two, with a parameter entering both linearly and quadratically (way 5). Closest known: rows proportional or in AP give a zero determinant. Different because: the dependence is among polynomials, not among the visible rows, and it fixes k through a quadratic equation.
blueprint_concepts: Determinant when a row is a linear combination of the others

concept_use.Determinant when a row is a linear combi: The determinant vanishes exactly when the third row (values of r) is a linear combination of the first two, i.e. r = lambda p + mu q; this gives k^2 + k - 2 = 0.

stem_review: Read as a student: p, q, r defined on R with the parameter k introduced first; the determinant is written in full; 'sum of all real values' is clear since there are two. Checked with sympy: determinant -2(k-1)(k+2). Answer -1 at (A) as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: Determinant zero iff r is a combination of p and q, which gives k^2 + k - 2 = 0.
justification: Routine: either expand a 3x3 determinant with a quadratic parameter or use the linear-dependence view, then Vieta; several standard steps, no new idea. Comparable to 2025-P1-Q1 (L2).
